title: Language and translation registry
coverage_statement: This archive snapshot bundles canon-linked reader records for Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, Ruth, Psalms, Amos, Joel, Obadiah, Jonah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Malachi, Book of Joshua the Son of Sirac plus 14 separately registered translation/companion layers. This is an availability count from reader records in this build, not a certification of completeness or textual accuracy; see each reader's review status. It records 28 language/script profile(s); these are scoped records, not an exhaustive world-language inventory. The coverage list contains 81 entries; 19 currently link to bundled source-text readers as canon-linked. 62 have no canon-linked reader here; 49 of those have a separately bundled research reader with an unverified Church-list link, while 13 have neither a canon-linked reader nor a bundled title-candidate research reader in this archive. These counts describe this snapshot only, not whether editions exist elsewhere; they are not a claim that no edition exists elsewhere. Mapping assertions for those 19 entries are: 0 source-asserted, 19 reviewed matches, 0 uncertain, 0 related-work links, 0 explicitly not mapped, and 0 mixed or unrecorded. A source-asserted title link does not establish current edition identity, textual completeness, or accuracy. The registry also contains 162 unbundled translation, source-edition, or corpus leads. It also includes 740 separately scoped related research readers; they are not linked to or counted as Church-list book coverage. Unknown perspectives, text, boundaries, translation paths, and rights remain unresolved where the evidence does not establish them. Absence from this package means not bundled here; a zero is reported only for a defined, completed survey that found none; unassessed scope remains not surveyed or unknown, never zero by default. Machine-generated or unreviewed wording is not promoted to verified scripture, and missing texts or viewpoints are not synthesized.

availability_survey.scope: Inspected three named online provider catalogue pages: STEP Bible's English version section, Bible.com's English-language versions listing, and eBible.org's World English Bible edition record. All three expose English Bible text/version availability. result_count is the number of provider pages inspected (3), not the number of distinct translations, books, complete Bibles, or all English scripture resources. availability_survey.notes: English text resources are also bundled elsewhere in this archive, including Brenton's 1851 English translation of the Greek Septuagint; that witness is not translated from the accompanying Geʽez texts, and matching labels do not prove alignment. languages.script_profile_note: Tigrinya is reported with Ethiopic script in the cited Eritrea literacy sources. The profile describes writing-system context, not a claim that every Tigrinya witness uses the same orthography.

availability_survey.scope: Checked YouVersion/Bible.com public Tigrinya (tir) language listing and the two version profiles it lists, TIG24 and TME15, for listed title, publisher, Tigrinya labeling, and visible book/chapter navigation. This is a bounded provider-page inventory only; it is not a census of Tigrinya scripture, an audit of either version’s complete book/chapter contents, an EOTC canon crosswalk, or a reuse-rights review. Also searched the eBible.org public Bible List and Study Text index for Tigrinya and Tigre. This provider-index check is discovery-only and is not treated as a complete catalogue survey.
availability_survey.notes: The result_count of two applies only to the inspected Bible.com Tigrinya versions page (TIG24 and TME15), not all providers. A separate Tigrinya website has an indexed homepage excerpt advertising scan/text access and 39 Old Testament plus 27 New Testament navigation entries; it is recorded as an unbundled lead with unidentified edition and rights, not included in the Bible.com count, not linked to an EOTC canon, and not treated as proof of a complete text. Other providers and editions remain unsurveyed. A separate Digital Bible Society Tigrinya profile lists a 1998 Genesis portion attributed to the Bible Society of Eritrea. Its separate 133-page Tigrinya Common Language Bible PDF identifies Bible Society of Ethiopia copyright and displays a contents list of the 27 standard New Testament books, although the generated PDF metadata describes a full Bible. These items are not assumed to be the same edition, and the PDF is not counted in the survey's two Bible.com edition result; no text is bundled because reuse permission and complete scope are not established. See SRC-331–SRC-332. The GitHub repository's XML header for AmharicTigrinya2024Bible.xml was inspected by a limited byte-range read. It identifies ‘Amharic (Tigrigna: Contemporary Tigrinya Bible 2024)’, embeds a Bible.com TIG24 link, and states ©2024 City Bible Foundation, used with permission, all rights reserved worldwide. This links the file to the sampled TIG24 edition (SRC-088–SRC-089) and conflicts with the repository README's Public Domain label; the separate MIT license covers software, not the scripture text. The repository table and XML translation label conflict on language, and the full file's contents and book/chapter inventory have not been audited. No text is copied; rights classification is permission-limited pending authorization, with no EOTC or Eritrean Orthodox crosswalk asserted (SRC-355). A separate BibleFactory listing describes the Tigrinya Contemporary Bible 2024 (BBTI7000) as a 720-page Old and New Testament product. Its seven-page New Testament sample identifies City Bible Foundation and says ‘All rights reserved worldwide’; this does not grant redistribution permission. The book list and contents of the complete product were not inspected, and no Orthodox canon crosswalk is asserted. A Tigrigna Bible App's indexed description separately claims text, scans, audio, and 66 books, but direct page retrieval exposed only an HTML shell, so that service's edition and inventory remain unverified and are not conflated with BBTI7000. Neither source adds bundled reader text or canon coverage. See SRC-369–SRC-371.  The eBible.org Bible List and Study Text index were also checked on 2026-10-26; searches for the names Tigrinya and Tigre returned no matching index text (SRC-399). This is a bounded negative finding only. It does not prove that no Tigrinya material exists at eBible.org or elsewhere; alternate names, unindexed files, and catalogue omissions remain possible. It adds no reader, text, or canon mapping. A bounded inspection of eBible.org's public scripture text index on 2026-10-27 found no exact ‘Tigrinya’, ‘Tigrigna’, ‘TIR’, or ‘Eritrea’ match in the returned index text. This describes only that provider index at inspection time; it is not evidence that open Tigrinya scripture is unavailable elsewhere, nor a complete search of its related links. No text was copied. The separate About page describes eBible.org's own redistributable materials and does not grant rights in third-party translations (SRC-437). A Four Corners of the World Library catalogue describes a 2000 Tigrinya Bible Society of Eritrea edition with deuterocanonical books, associates it with the Eritrean Orthodox Tewahdo Church, and reports cross-church participation. The volume itself was not inspected; its complete book list, translation basis, EOTC 81-entry mapping, and reuse rights remain unverified. It is retained as an unmapped print-edition lead, not bundled text or an Orthodox canon crosswalk (SRC-438).

languages.script_profile_note: This [ar] profile carries a bounded eBible.org resource survey filtered by Eritrea. availability_survey.scope: Inspected eBible.org's Eritrea-filtered territory catalogue and the three Arabic edition records it links: Van Dyck, WBTC Easy Reading Version, and Biblica Open New Arabic Version. The result_count of three is the number of Arabic-labeled edition rows on that one country-filtered catalogue, not a count of Eritrean-specific translations, Arabic varieties, or all scripture resources. All three edition records identify standard Arabic [arb], not a distinct Eritrean Arabic witness. Separate Joshua Project country and language-profile pages report Arabic varieties associated with Eritrean people groups, including Hijazi Arabic [acw] and a Bible-Portions status; this is secondary composite discovery data, not direct text verification or a crosswalk to the three standard-Arabic editions. Glottolog lists Hijazi Arabic's countries as Saudi Arabia and Yemen, while Joshua Project associates Rashaida in Eritrea with that code; the discrepancy remains unresolved. The survey is bounded to these cited pages; it is not a census or rights/completeness/accuracy review.
availability_survey.notes: The profile label Arabic (Eritrea) is country-context metadata under the general BCP 47 Arabic tag [ar], not a claim that Eritrea has one distinct Arabic language or that standard-Arabic editions are local community translations. The eBible.org catalogue's country filter establishes that its listed versions are offered in its Eritrea index, not their adoption, accessibility, or ecclesial status in Eritrea. The three editions have different reuse notices; none is bundled here. Joshua Project's Hijazi entry is retained as a separate, secondary discovery lead; its reported portions were not obtained or audited. Glottolog's Hijazi Arabic profile does not list Eritrea, so the Eritrea association remains unresolved between these sources and is not adopted as settled language geography.

availability_survey.scope: Inspected the Scripture Earth Blin (byn) resource listing, the Digital Bible Society BYNEWT record and its linked 1890 Mark scan, and two publication reports concerning the 2018 Blin New Testament launch. The bounded result count is two digital resource listings, not two translations or complete editions. The 1890 Mark item is bundled as an 80-page Ethiopic-script facsimile; the provider's Latin script label conflicts with the scan. Its Tesseract OCR is retained only as an unusable diagnostic, not as reader text. The reported 2018 New Testament is a separate modern edition and remains unbundled. This survey does not establish the complete present-day Blin corpus, the scope or rights of the modern edition, an EOTC or Eritrean Orthodox canon crosswalk, or the accuracy/completeness of the 1890 scan.
availability_survey.notes: The 1890 scan was retrieved from the exact PDF linked by DBS and retained with the original IA metadata, OCR derivative, and scan data. DBS/Find a Bible labels it Public Domain / OPEN; IA metadata says the contributor is unaware of restrictions. This is recorded as a provider-stated rights claim. The scan is available as a local facsimile; no text transcription was created. Its rendered Ethiopic script conflicts with the DBS record's Latin script field. The OCR settings omit the byn language, identify it as invalid, and misclassify the text as Kazakh/Cyrillic, so the OCR is not suitable as scripture text. The modern 2018 Blin New Testament reports do not identify a public digital text or reuse license. See SRC-303–SRC-307 and SRC-339.

edition_leads.title: Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (Book of Clement), Eritrean manuscript tradition
edition_leads.edition_statement: Alessandro Bausi's 2024 study identifies the Ethiopic Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957) and discusses an Eritrean manuscript documented by the Missione Italiana in Eritrea in 1992 and revisited in 2019. The reported witness is parchment, at latest fifteenth century, 166 folios, damaged, and has a nonstandard sequence of books.
edition_leads.scope_description: Discovery candidate for Church-list entry eotc-nt-34 (“Book of Clement”) because the scholarly name is also translated “Book of Clement”; the Church list does not give the Geʽez title, so the crosswalk remains uncertain. Bausi describes Qalemǝnṭos as a seven-book Ethiopic work, distinct from the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter, only partially corresponding to the Arabic Apocalypse of Peter to Clement. Do not conflate this with the three Epistles of Clement counted together in one broader-canon account (SRC-073), or with the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter (CAe 317). No comprehensive critical edition exists; existing French and Italian translations cover different portions. No manuscript images, transcription, or scripture text are bundled.
edition_leads.rights_status: The cited scholarly chapter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; that license applies to the article, not to the Qalemǝnṭos manuscript or translations it discusses. Rights of the witness and French, Italian, and Geʽez–Amharic editions are not established; no text is bundled.
edition_leads.review_status: Bausi 2024 chapter inspected in full. It reports a seven-book work and complementary French/Italian translations, but the Church-list crosswalk, manuscript completeness, exact text editions, and rights of the underlying scripture or translations remain unresolved. No text bundled.

edition_leads.scope_description: Uncertain candidate for Church-list entry eotc-ot-20 (“I Maccabees”). This supports a historical title-family connection to the Church list’s “I Maccabees” / “II and III Maccabees” grouping, but not a verified text or edition crosswalk. Cowley warns that canon-list labels do not uniquely identify texts. Do not treat the BL Oriental 506 manuscript as a confirmed witness to this printed edition. No text bundled.

edition_leads.scope_description: The Internet Archive hosts a scan of Patrologia Orientalis volume 2, and the Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal bibliography identifies Pereira’s Ethiopic Job contribution within it. CiNii’s later-edition record identifies French and Geʽez text languages and Geʽez as the original language. This metadata does not establish the exact boundaries or completeness of the Ethiopic text in the scanned 1907 volume. The Church’s cited English list separately includes Job as entry 22; this candidate link is not a verified witness-to-canon mapping.
edition_leads.rights_status: Internet Archive catalog metadata reports “Possible copyright status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT” and an evidence note of no visible copyright notice, with stated date 1907 [i.e. 1903]. edition_leads.review_status: Bibliographic metadata and IA catalog fields inspected only. IA reports French OCR detection, which does not establish usable Ethiopic OCR. The scan, Ethiopic text boundaries, chapter/section sequence, completeness, mapping, and reuse terms remain unreviewed.

edition_leads.title: Ethiopic Book of Rebukes (Tegsats) — reported section of Pilkington thesis

edition_leads.scope_description: Oxford's thesis abstract describes a critical edition whose base text is Cambridge University Library Add. 1570, collated against 21 Ethiopic manuscripts and two printed sources, with a literal English translation of the base text. The thesis PDFs and those pages remain uninspected; the index's page/section claim, chapter range, completeness, and relation to the Church-listed Tegsats are unverified; the thesis abstract alone does not verify that the thesis section is the Church-listed work. This is an edition lead, not bundled coverage.
edition_leads.rights_status: Oxford metadata identifies Pilkington as copyright holder and gives 1978 copyright metadata. Reuse terms for the thesis files and text have not been established; obtain permission or review the repository terms and applicable rights before copying or adapting. No text is copied.
edition_leads.review_status: The Oxford repository record and abstract were inspected. They support the thesis identity, base manuscript, stated collation scope, and the author's report of a literal English rendering. The secondary-index pointer to pp. 318–522 is not independently confirmed in the thesis. Exact Tegsats boundaries, thesis text content, completeness, reuse terms, and Church-list identity remain unreviewed.

edition_leads.title: Te’ezaz section of Ethiopic Sinodos — Horner 1904 image edition
edition_leads.edition_statement: Tel Aviv University identifies its page-image version as the Te'ezaz part of the Ethiopic Sinodos, following George Horner (ed.), The Statutes of the Apostles (London, 1904). The project links an Internet Archive scan of the related Horner volume; Internet Archive says this specific scan is without the Ethiopic and Arabic texts included in the complete 1904 edition, so it is not the Geez witness. The IA OCR contents list an English translation of the Ethiopic text from printed p. 127 and the Arabic translation from p. 233 (provisional English locator: pp. 127-232; page images were not collated). This range does not verify a Te'ezaz crosswalk or its boundaries. Cowley reports Te'ezaz as 71 or 72 canons and printed in Horner 1904; Mikre-Sellassie reports 71 and cites Horner. The OCR contents place the Ethiopic translation at printed p. 127 and the Arabic translation at p. 233; treat pp. 127–232 as a provisional locator, not a verified Te'ezaz boundary. Cowley reports Te'ezaz as 71 or 72 canons and printed in Horner 1904; Mikre-Sellassie reports 71 and cites Horner. Horner's contents call printed pp. 127–232 'Translation of the Ethiopic' and begin 'Translation of the Arabic' at p. 233. These are translation-section locators in Horner's broader Statutes volume, not verified boundaries for the Church-list Tizaz entry. The Internet Archive scan is a separate English-language digitization and explicitly omits the Ethiopic and Arabic text witnesses.
edition_leads.scope_description: Cowley reports Te'ezaz as one of four apostolically attributed Sinodos sections, gives a count of 71 or 72 canons, and says it was printed in Horner 1904 (SRC-210). Mikre-Sellassie independently reports 71 canons and cites Horner (SRC-441). Horner's contents identify its English translation of the Ethiopic at printed pp. 127–232 and the Arabic translation beginning at p. 233; these are section locators in Horner's broader Statutes volume, not verified boundaries for Church-list Tizaz. The scan OCR includes headings for Statutes 71 and 72, but the full sequence has not been audited. The linked Internet Archive copy explicitly lacks the Ethiopic and Arabic text witnesses (SRC-368). TAU identifies its external page images as the Te'ezaz section following Horner and reports that printed pages 5, 9, 17, 21, 25, 35, 41, 49, 53, 60, 70, and 71 seem missing in that edition (SRC-213). This is TAU's warning about its hosted edition, not proof that those pages are absent from every witness. Horner's contents identify the English translation of the Ethiopic on pp. 127-232 and the Arabic translation from p. 233; this is a section boundary within Horner's volume, not a verified boundary for the Church-list Tizaz entry. These sources support a strong research association, but this is not an authoritative crosswalk: the modern Church-list spelling/gloss ‘Tizaz (the book of Herald)’ has not been reconciled against a Church text witness; manuscript contents vary, and the 71/72 count differs across reports. Keep the mapping provisional; no text, images, exact boundaries, or reuse permissions are asserted.
edition_leads.rights_status: No text or images are copied. The 1904 edition's age suggests historical public-domain status in some jurisdictions, but the TAU image site's terms, underlying source scan terms, and any transcription reuse conditions have not been verified. Internet Archive separately shows 'Possible copyright status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT' for the US-region item metadata; this is not worldwide clearance or a legal determination, and does not settle reuse terms for TAU's images or extracted text. No public-domain or open-license claim is made.
edition_leads.review_status: Rechecked 2026-10-27: TAU's information page identifies its hosted Ge'ez images as Te'ezaz and reports missing printed pages; Cowley reports Te'ezaz with 71 or 72 canons and links it to Horner 1904; Mikre-Sellassie reports 71 and cites Horner. Horner's contents identify an English translation of the Ethiopic at printed pp. 127-232 and Arabic from p. 233; this is a section boundary within the broader Statutes volume, not a verified Church-list Tizaz boundary. IA metadata says this separate English-language scan lacks the Ethiopic and Arabic text witnesses. The OCR contains headings for Statutes 71 and 72, but the full sequence has not been audited. These sources strengthen the work association but do not reconcile the Church-list gloss/spelling, manuscript variation, exact boundaries, missing pages, translation accuracy, completeness, or reuse rights. No text or images were copied or bundled.
